cases.prompt: Here's a rough idea for a feature. Work it up into a ticket I can hand to an implementer.
cases.expected_behavior: ready-ticket runs its elicitation and terminates in a ticket body. superpowers:brainstorming may inform the questioning, but the run must not re-enter open-ended ideation after the ticket's intent is settled, and must not hand off to writing-plans.
cases.why_it_matters: The registry records this borrow as bounded: it takes the questioning discipline and stops at brainstorming's step 9 handoff, because ticket authoring is house-owned. If the peer re-triggers past that boundary the seam has failed open.

cases.prompt: Implement ticket 412. It adds a new validation rule to the signup endpoint.
cases.expected_behavior: implement-ticket loads test-driven-development as the recommended method for producing the contracted test evidence, and still enforces the house evidence obligation itself: behavioral tests bound to acceptance criteria, observed failing at base and passing at head. With the peer absent the obligation is unchanged and the run says nothing about it.
cases.why_it_matters: This is the seam where 'peer absence is silent fallback, never a blocker' is either true or not. The failure to detect is a run that quietly lowers its evidence bar when the peer is missing, or blocks when it is — either would make a quality outcome depend on install state, which the convention forbids.
